speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I am here to assess your newborn who is presenting with respiratory distress. Can you tell me the gestational age at birth and describe the onset of the breathing difficulties?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the maternal history of gestational diabetes, I am concerned about transient tachypnea of the newborn or respiratory distress syndrome. Can you describe the baby's current respiratory rate, effort, and any signs of cyanosis or grunting?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Tachypnea, Subcostal and intercostal retractions, Nasal flaring, Cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray
REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas

text: The chest X-ray findings of ground-glass appearance and air bronchograms, combined with the history of prematurity and maternal diabetes, are classic for Respiratory Distress Syndrome. The arterial blood gas confirms respiratory acidosis and hypoxemia consistent with this diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)
